$comment: TXT export and import (feature 017): File > Export > Export as TXT..., File > Import > TXT File..., File > Open's refusal of a TXT, the export's options and its own options window, the settings of Settings > Exports for TXT and the summaries. Feature catalogue merged into en.json by i18n/index.ts.

exportTxt.description: Write the book as a plain text file: a title page, the text with its notes, and a record of the description at the end, in UTF-8 or an encoding of the book's language

importTxt.description: Make a new book from a plain text file: its paragraphs in one body; the editor's own TXT files give their description and notes back

txt.openRefused: {{path}} is a text file. File > Open takes FictionBook (FB2) books, FBD files and ZIP archives holding FB2 books; a text file is imported with File > Import > TXT File....
txt.openRefusedInArchive: {{path}} holds a text file but no FictionBook book. A text file is imported with File > Import > TXT File....
txt.exportCancelled: The TXT export was cancelled; nothing was written.
txt.ownFile: it is the book's own file, or the archive it was opened from.

summary.intro: Some characters cannot be written in {{encoding}}:
summary.noTitle: The book has no title; the file's name "{{detail}}" stands in for it.
summary.unread: The record's value "{{detail}}" could not be read; the template's stands.
summary.fbd: The description, cover included, was taken from {{name}}.

txt.importCancelled: The TXT import was cancelled; the book in the window is as it was.

refused.binary: it is not a text file.
refused.fictionBook: it is a FictionBook book - open it with File > Open.
refused.noTxtInArchive: the archive holds no TXT file.
refused.damaged: the file or the archive cannot be read.
refused.encrypted: the archive is protected by a password.
refused.tooLargeEntry: the archive's file is too large.

fbd.none: None - keep the description the TXT gives

txt.fbdUnreadable: {{name}} cannot be read ({{reason}}); the book comes in without it.

txt.encoding: The encoding the text is written in; UTF-8 writes every character
txt.bom: Begin a UTF-8 file with the byte-order mark some Windows programs look for
txt.zip: Write a ZIP archive with the TXT file and an FBD file of the book's description and cover
txt.importEncoding: The encoding the text file was written in; the most likely first

txt.mode: Which encoding the TXT export's dialog proposes for a book's first export
txt.encoding: The encoding proposed for books in this language
txt.bom: Whether the dialog proposes the byte-order mark for UTF-8 files
txt.zip: Whether the dialog proposes a ZIP archive with the TXT and the book's FBD
txt.includePictures: Whether the one-file Markdown export proposes to include the pictures
txt.pdfZip: Whether the PDF export's dialog proposes a ZIP archive with the PDF and the book's FBD
